title: A code item's landing runs its checks once and leaves the lookup check to the gate's mapped tests
goal: backlog.py land's second pass (after the code/<id> request merged) writes done's evidence from the first pass's checks step, kept with the blobs of the item's touched files at the pushed code/<id> tip, when those files hold the same blobs at the merged main, and runs the checks again only when one differs; land runs its rag.py lookup step only when the sync gate's selection lacks test_kb_lookup.py, which runs the same lookup set, and the contract lint stays; planted cases: unchanged touched files reuse the first pass's results, a touched file changed by another merge reruns the checks, a landing whose gate selection lacks test_kb_lookup.py keeps the lookup step

gates.question: May done's evidence for a code item come from the checks land ran before the merge request, when the item's touched files are unchanged after the merge, and may land skip its lookup step when the gate's selection holds test_kb_lookup.py? reuse = both; rerun-checks = keep running the checks at done, skip only the redundant lookup step; keep = today (checks at step checks and again at done, the lookup step on every landing that changes _tools/)

notes: Premise (run before a sprint commits it): python3 -c "import json,glob; r=[json.loads(l) for f in glob.glob('kb/_querylog/ops/*/*.jsonl') for l in open(f,encoding='utf-8') if '\"land.step\"' in l]; c={x['item'] for x in r if x['step']=='checks'}; d={x['item'] for x in r if x['step']=='done'}; print(len(c & d), 'items ran their checks at step checks and again at step done')" prints 13 (5 real items, the rest fixture rows from before BG-5pz44tdi). Data, committed ops rows of real items: step checks median 9.4 s (n=7), step done median 4.3 s (n=97, p90 29.5 s; 9.8 s for the 5 code items), the lookup step median 4.0 s (n=113), lint 0.3 s, on macOS; over 46 items done since 2026-10-03, their checks hit 1 or 2 test files, 48 of 50 inside the gate's own mapped selection (a median 1.4% of it). On the Windows host each tests.py -k run collects the whole suite (about 6 s in one process, 13.5 s under xdist) and the lookup step takes 5.3 s warm, 21.2 s cold (kb/_self/reports/test-suite-speed.md): an estimated 1 to 2 min per code landing there, 15 to 30 s on macOS. Small: P3.
